stories.title: Rescuers continue grim search for Nepal flood survivors
stories.summary: Rescuers in Nepal continue searching for survivors after floods killed over 1,300 people and left more than 5,500 missing, with ongoing efforts in tunnels where workers may still be trapped. Two hydropower workers were miraculously rescued after nine days trapped in debris, boosting the morale of rescue teams working alongside international experts. Prime Minister Balendra Shah pledged to improve living conditions for thousands displaced, while mass graves are used for over 1,000 victims due to overwhelmed morgues. Inspired by the “miracle” rescue of two hydropower workers, Nepal’s emergency response teams were digging with new vigour on Sept 5 through piles of debris as the death toll from the flooding disaster crossed 1,200. The rescued pair were among hundreds of hydropower workers who went missing since a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through the China-Nepal border following a vast glacial and rock collapse on Aug 26. So far, 1,294 bodies have been recovered in Nepal, according to the disaster agency, with 5,053 people missing. In China, state media said 31 people had been killed and 531 were missing. That takes the overall death toll to 1,325 people, with 5,584 missing. “We have been working since morning on search and rescue operations,” Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP on Sept 5. Searches continued at the Trishuli 3A tunnel where the two men were rescued on Sept 4, as well as multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects destroyed by the floods. “Work is also underway at the tunnels,” Basnet said. “We don’t have an update yet, but the work goes on.”
